business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Backward integration for quality control and sustainability: primary raw material is copper rods made from copper cathodes; the Company has backward-integrated its manufacturing facility to produce oxygen-free copper rods from copper cathodes in-house. About 35%-40% of total copper rod requirement was manufactured in-house from copper cathodes during the three months period ended June 30, 2025 and the last 3 Fiscals, with the remainder purchased from suppliers. Raw material requirements are met through a mix of imports and local procurement; imports constituted about 30%-56% of total raw material requirements during the three months period ended June 30, 2025 and the last 3 Fiscals. Major raw material suppliers include Vedanta Limited, Marubeni Corporation, Union Copper Rod LLC, Hindalco Industries Ltd., Bharat Aluminium Company Ltd. and Ducab Metals LLC, with over ten years of relationship maintained with Vedanta Limited, Union Copper Rod LLC and Hindalco Industries Ltd.

internal_operational.evidence: Copper Rod/Cathode cost: ₹3,666.20mn (92.09% of purchases) Q1FY26; ₹12,987.43mn (93.87%) FY25; ₹10,834.31mn (96.51%) FY24; ₹9,127.51mn (96.19%) FY23. Aluminium Rod: 1.82%-3.06% of purchases across periods.
internal_operational.title: Raw material price/supply volatility (copper, aluminium, insulation materials)

internal_operational.detail: Company is subject to inspection/pre-qualification audits by customers who assess operating facilities before placing orders; requires UL approval for exports to the USA; some prospective customers have not placed orders post-audit in the past.
internal_operational.evidence: Successful conversion of pre-qualification audit to orders: 70.00% (Q1FY26), 78.57% (FY25), 70.00% (FY24), 100.00% (FY23).
internal_operational.title: Customer pre-qualification and pre-order audits

internal_operational.detail: Continuous operation of Anand, Gujarat manufacturing facilities is critical; facilities subject to equipment/power breakdown, labour disputes, natural disasters, and industrial accidents.
internal_operational.evidence: 'While there has been no such stoppage, breakdown or shutdown of plant and machinery during the three months period ended June 30, 2025, and the last 5 Fiscals, we cannot assure you that such instances will not occur in the future.'
internal_operational.title: Manufacturing facility disruption/breakdown risk

internal_operational.detail: Copper-based products (enamelled copper winding wires/strips, paper insulated copper conductors, bare copper wire/rod, PV ribbon copper) contribute over 93% of revenue; any slowdown in copper product demand would adversely impact the business.
internal_operational.title: High revenue concentration in copper-based products (>93%)

internal_operational.detail: Company does not have formal long-term agreements for supply of products or raw materials with most suppliers/customers, despite long-standing relationships with several.
internal_operational.evidence: % of customers having long-term relationship: 30.50% (Q1FY26), 21.17% (FY25), 20.38% (FY24), 21.41% (FY23); % of raw material suppliers having long-term relationship: 15.15%, 6.67%, 7.69%, 7.04% respectively. Top 5 customers contributed 16.74%-23.76% of total sales across periods.
internal_operational.title: No long-term agreements with most raw material suppliers/customers

internal_operational.detail: Company is dependent on its top 5 suppliers for most raw material supplies; top 2 suppliers (Vedanta Limited and Marubeni Corporation) collectively contributed over 60% of total purchases in each period; disputes with these suppliers could disrupt raw material supply.
internal_operational.evidence: Top 1 supplier: 34.75%-42.32% of purchases across periods. Top 5 suppliers: 89.82% (Q1FY26), 86.26% (FY25), 89.27% (FY24), 82.21% (FY23) of purchases. Top 10 suppliers: 92.81%-94.66% of purchases.
internal_operational.title: Dependence on top raw material suppliers, especially Vedanta Limited and Marubeni Corporation

internal_operational.detail: Domestic revenue is concentrated in the western states of Gujarat and Maharashtra; any slowdown or disturbance in these states may impact business.
internal_operational.title: Revenue concentration in western India (Gujarat & Maharashtra)

internal_operational.detail: Company is largely dependent on third-party transportation providers (in addition to owned trucks) to move raw materials and finished products, with no long-term agreements entered into with such providers; transporter damages may not be enforceable against them.
internal_operational.evidence: 'We don't enter into any long-term agreement with such entities.' Transportation costs have steadily increased in the past.
internal_operational.title: Dependence on third-party transportation providers

internal_operational.detail: Exports are subject to country-specific economic, political, regulatory, and currency risks; established competitors in international markets may have stronger distributor/customer relationships.
internal_operational.title: Export risk across 18+ countries and 5 continents

internal_operational.detail: Raw materials, work-in-progress, and finished goods stored at operating facilities; improper storage/handling could reduce raw material quality and damage work products.
internal_operational.evidence: 'While we have not faced any such situation during the three months period ended June 30, 2025, and Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023, however we cannot assure you that such instances will not occur in future.'
internal_operational.title: Improper storage/handling could damage raw materials and inventory

internal_operational.detail: While majority of products are manufactured against confirmed orders, fluctuations in demand could affect inventory levels, resulting in write-downs/write-offs or, conversely, inability to meet excess demand.
internal_operational.evidence: Factors affecting forecast accuracy cited: substantial demand swings, changing customer requirements, aggressive competitor pricing, limited historical data in newer markets, FX fluctuations, weakening economic conditions.
internal_operational.title: Demand forecasting and inventory fluctuation risk

internal_operational.detail: Operating processes are labour intensive; Company employs a mix of permanent and contractual employees and depends on third-party labour contractors; high attrition raises training/recruitment costs.
internal_operational.evidence: As of November 14, 2025: 139 permanent employees and 394 contractual employees. Attrition rate: 7.69% (Q1FY26), 23.82% (FY25), 13.76% (FY24), 12.67% (FY23).
internal_operational.title: Manpower-intensive operations, labour laws, and attrition

internal_operational.detail: Registered office and manufacturing facilities are situated on land leased from Gujarat Industrial Development Corporation (GIDC) and other lessors; one Bhiwandi warehouse is occupied on a no-objection-certificate basis without a formal lease agreement; lease termination could require relocation.
internal_operational.evidence: Leased properties include: Plot No. 8/1-2 GIDC (lease from March 31, 1987, ₹100,000/annum), Plot No. 123/B GIDC (from October 26, 1970, ₹20,000/annum), Warehousing plot (from October 28, 1970, ₹30,000/annum), Windmill land at Rajkot (from October 9, 2020, ₹1,400,000/annum). Bhiwandi warehouse occupied via NOC without formal lease.
internal_operational.title: Operations conducted on leased land

internal_operational.detail: Operations require handling hazardous/heated/flammable materials; subject to risk of explosions, fires, mechanical failures, and other operational hazards that could cause personal injury or property damage.
internal_operational.evidence: 'While we have not experienced any such significant hazards in the past which caused any personal injury or destruction to property.' No lawsuits/claims during Q1FY26 and Fiscals 2025, 2024, 2023.
internal_operational.title: Hazardous materials and workplace safety hazards

internal_operational.detail: Company is subject to ISO 14001:2015 and ISO 9001:2015 quality certification requirements; instances in the past of products being returned by customers for not meeting requirements, exposing the Company to potential product liability claims.
internal_operational.evidence: Reject/returned goods vs revenue from operations (₹ million): Q1FY26 0.55 vs 4,117.58; FY25 2.01 vs 14,863.9; FY24 3.07 vs 11,809.0; FY23 4.33 vs 10,085.3.
internal_operational.title: Product quality/defects and customer returns

internal_operational.detail: Business strategy, direction, and customer relationships are substantially dependent on Promoters and Key Managerial Personnel; loss of, or inability to attract/retain, such persons could materially adversely affect operations.
internal_operational.evidence: Narrative risk factor; no company-specific quantification provided in this text.
internal_operational.title: Dependence on Promoters and KMP

internal_operational.detail: Backward integration of manufacturing enables cost/time efficiency and quality control; disruptions could force sourcing of components from third-party suppliers at unfavorable rates, timelines, or volumes.
internal_operational.evidence: Narrative risk factor; no company-specific quantification provided.
internal_operational.title: Backward integration underutilization risk

internal_operational.detail: Installed manufacturing capacity and capacity utilization figures are based on management assumptions and estimates regarding raw material availability, quality, and operational efficiency; future utilization may vary significantly.
internal_operational.evidence: Capacity certificates obtained from independent chartered engineer J B Mistry & Co.
internal_operational.title: Installed capacity/utilization based on management assumptions

internal_operational.detail: Company maintains insurance for property, stock, money, transit, and product liability, but policies are subject to standard limitations and may not cover all potential losses.
internal_operational.evidence: Insurance coverage as % of insurable assets: 279.61% (Q1FY26), 244.15% (FY25), 170.50% (FY24), 138.88% (FY23); sum insured ₹3,764.38mn vs insurable assets ₹1,346.28mn as at Q1FY26.
internal_operational.title: Insurance coverage may be inadequate

internal_operational.detail: Operations depend on information technology systems susceptible to malfunction from equipment damage, power outages, computer viruses, and hardware/software/network problems.
internal_operational.evidence: 'While we have not faced any major issues in the past, we cannot assure you that such issue will not occur in the future.'
internal_operational.title: IT systems failure/disruption risk

strategy_growth.detail: Use of Net Proceeds has not been appraised by any external independent agency, bank, or financial institution and is based on management estimates that may change with market conditions.
strategy_growth.evidence: 'The objects of the Fresh Issue and deployment of funds have not been appraised by any external agency or any bank or financial institution or any other independent agency and are based on management estimates.'
strategy_growth.title: Objects of Fresh Issue/fund deployment based on unappraised management estimates

strategy_growth.detail: Company has placed orders for only part of the plant and machinery to be funded from Net Proceeds, exposing it to time/cost overrun risk on the remaining unordered equipment.
strategy_growth.evidence: 'We have already placed orders for certain plant and machinery aggregating to ₹228.42 million... orders for the remaining portion of the total capital expenditure towards the purchase of plant and machinery are yet to be placed.'
strategy_growth.title: Plant & machinery purchase orders partly unplaced

strategy_growth.detail: Industry is fragmented with unbranded players enjoying a price advantage; Company competes on product quality/reliability, technical/production capability, delivery, and price against established players.
strategy_growth.evidence: 'As per the CareEdge Report, the market share of the Company for Fiscal 2025 is 5.7%.' Key competitors named: Precision Wires India Limited, Ram Ratna Wires Limited, Apar Industries Limited.
strategy_growth.title: Competitive pressures in the winding and conductivity products industry

strategy_growth.detail: Any variation in the disclosed use of Net Proceeds requires shareholder special resolution and a dissenting-shareholder exit offer from Promoters, potentially limiting the Company's flexibility to redeploy funds.
strategy_growth.evidence: Narrative; governed by Companies Act, 2013 and SEBI ICDR Regulations Schedule XX.
strategy_growth.title: Restrictions on variation of Net Proceeds utilization

strategy_growth.detail: Success of the business depends on effectively managing expansion projects and implementing strategy; execution depends on financing availability/terms, regulatory approvals, and general economic conditions.
strategy_growth.evidence: Narrative; no company-specific figures provided in this extract.
strategy_growth.title: Execution risk on business strategy/expansion plans

strategy_growth.detail: Changes in client preferences, regulatory requirements, or competing technologies could render products obsolete; no assurance the Company can secure the technological knowledge needed to remain competitive.
strategy_growth.title: Failure to anticipate evolving industry trends/new product development

strategy_growth.detail: Changes in Indian trade policies, treaties, and tariffs (or those of countries the Company imports from/exports to) could increase operating costs and reduce competitiveness.
strategy_growth.evidence: 'the lapse of anti-dumping duty on polyvinyl chloride imports from China in 2022.'
strategy_growth.title: Trade policy/tariff changes affecting profitability

strategy_growth.detail: A change in government or reversal of India's economic liberalization/deregulation policies could adversely affect business and economic conditions generally.
strategy_growth.title: Political instability/reversal of economic liberalization

strategy_growth.detail: Cyclones, floods, earthquakes, pandemics, terrorism, military actions, and civil unrest could adversely affect operations, financial condition, and Indian securities markets generally.
strategy_growth.evidence: Narrative; references India's history of natural calamities and civil disturbances.
strategy_growth.title: Natural/man-made disasters, terrorism, and civil unrest

strategy_growth.detail: Acts of violence or war involving India, or deterioration in relations with neighbouring countries, could negatively affect investor confidence and the trading price of the Equity Shares.
strategy_growth.title: Terrorist attacks/civil unrest affecting Indian securities markets

strategy_growth.detail: Enumerated external risks that could affect business, operations, and market price of Equity Shares if they materialise, including FX/interest rate changes, forex reserve decline, political instability, civil unrest, credit scarcity, sovereign rating downgrades, tax policy changes, and natural/man-made calamities including pandemics.
strategy_growth.evidence: Nine bulleted external risk factors listed under Risk Factor 73 in the RHP text.
strategy_growth.title: Broad regulatory/economic/political uncertainty (India-specific external factors)
